digest.component_or_area: Git fetch coordination in rebar._store and rebar._snapshot
propositions: Concurrent Git fetches against a shared Git common directory fail with 'cannot lock ref refs/remotes/origin/tickets: is at <new> but expected <old>' when uncoordinated ref-update operations race on remote-tracking refs.

The sync fetch in rebar._store.sync.reconverge and snapshot fetch in rebar._snapshot.git_fetch.fetch_origin operate outside cross-process coordination, causing compare-and-swap failures on shared remote-tracking refs.

Controlled experiments demonstrate 82/128 stale-reference failures under parallel fetch execution versus zero failures under serialized execution, proving the race is a coordination defect not a transient network issue.

The existing per-worktree Git advisory lock does not coordinate fetch operations across multiple worktrees sharing one Git common directory, as it is keyed per-worktree and the fetch legs explicitly operate outside its domain.

Fetch operations must be coordinated by canonical Git common-directory identity with either cross-process locking or bounded retry of compare-and-swap failures, while preserving the requirement that fetches do not hold the ticket write lock.
